about: The conformance corpus the Node binding is held to. Every case is a MeTTa
source or a wire atom; nothing here records an expected answer, because
the shipped Python host supplies those at run time and a frozen copy of
them could go stale without anything noticing.
Numbers are written as their canonical Prolog text. JSON has one number
kind, so a JSON value cannot tell the integer 2 from the float 2.0, and
the engine tells them apart through pure term equality as well as identity:
Prolog reads the text into its own representation, Python into int and float
and JavaScript into BigInt and number. MeTTa's Number or BigInt type is
recovered from the exact integer value at the signed-i64 boundary.
Every case must answer the same in a fresh engine and in one that has
already run other work, because the Python host shares one engine per
pytest worker while the Node binding boots its own. A case that turns on
whether a library happens to be loaded compares two different engines: an
!(memoize f) case was here and answered true on one side and the
unreduced expression on the other, depending on which test file ran first.
This supplemental corpus compares live hosts. The golden corpus at
tests/codec/corpus.json separately holds both hosts to the wire grammar.
